root_cause.text: In `drivers/md/md-llbitmap.c`, `llbitmap_start_write()` and `llbitmap_start_discard()` called `llbitmap_state_machine()` before raising the per-page barrier, creating a race where state transitions could complete while the needed barrier protection was not yet in place.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `llbitmap_raise_barrier(llbitmap, page_start)` loop to occur before `llbitmap_state_machine(llbitmap, start, end, BitmapActionStartwrite/Discard)`, and the CVE text explicitly says this fixes the issue by “raise barrier before state machine transition” to prevent the state machine from completing before the barrier is properly raised.

agent_logs.evidence_points: The patch moves `llbitmap_raise_barrier(llbitmap, page_start)` loop to occur before `llbitmap_state_machine(llbitmap, start, end, BitmapActionStartwrite/Discard)`, and the CVE text explicitly says this fixes the issue by “raise barrier before state machine transition” to prevent the state machine from completing before the barrier is properly raised.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reorder write-start handling so bitmap page barriers are raised before the state machine processes the start-write transition.
intent_record.what: In llbitmap_start_write(), the call to llbitmap_state_machine(llbitmap, start, end, BitmapActionStartwrite) was moved from before the page barrier loop to after it. The barrier-raising while loop itself was left unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, page barriers are now raised before the bitmap state machine is notified of a write start. This changes the ordering of internal operations so that the write-protection/barrier state is established first, reducing the chance that the state machine observes or acts on the write-start transition before the relevant pages are protected.

intent_record.intent_summary: Reorder discard handling so page barriers are established before the bitmap discard state machine runs.
intent_record.what: In llbitmap_start_discard(), the call to llbitmap_state_machine(llbitmap, start, end, BitmapActionDiscard) was moved from before the page barrier loop to after it. The barrier-raising loop itself was left unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the code now raises barriers for all pages covering the discard range before triggering the discard state machine. This changes the ordering so the discard action is processed only after the relevant pages are protected, reducing the chance that discard handling races with page activity.

grouping_result.intent: Reorder discard handling so page barriers are established before the bitmap discard state machine runs.

relevance_review.reason: The changes directly match the root cause: they reorder llbitmap start-write/start-discard handling so the per-page barrier is raised before llbitmap_state_machine() processes the transition, fixing the race described.

candidates.rationale: This call processes the start-write transition before per-page barriers are raised, matching the root cause race where state transitions can complete without barrier protection.
This call processes the discard transition before per-page barriers are raised, which directly creates the race described in the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement invokes the start-write state machine before the per-page barrier is raised, allowing the transition to complete without the needed barrier protection.
This statement invokes the discard state machine before the per-page barrier is raised, creating the race where state transitions can finish without barrier protection.

In `llbitmap_start_write()` the code clearly calls `llbitmap_state_machine(llbitmap, start, end, BitmapActionStartwrite);` and only afterwards raises the per-page barrier in the `while (page_start <= page_end)` loop via `llbitmap_raise_barrier(llbitmap, page_start);`. Likewise, `llbitmap_start_discard()` does the same ordering: it calls `llbitmap_state_machine(llbitmap, start, end, BitmapActionDiscard);` before the barrier loop. This matches the root cause exactly: state transitions happen before barrier protection is established, creating the race. There is no evidence in these functions of the fix (no pre-barrier acquisition before the state machine call), so `is_fixed` is false.
